hard_case: A `#[macro_export]` generator in `tests/export_support/mod.rs` is named by `use crate::exported_table;` in another module of the same test crate; no `#[macro_use]` is involved and the middle row sits on the limit.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: 5 against a limit of 5 no longer fits
not equivalent: 6 against a limit of 5 now fits

reasoning: Rows export_under(3, 5, true), export_at(5, 5, true) and export_over(6, 5, false) sit under and on both sides of the limit, so `limit > width` fails export_at and `limit + 1 >= width` fails export_over. The generator `exported_table!` is `#[macro_export]` in tests/export_support/mod.rs and the invoking module names it with `use crate::exported_table;`, so ripr has to resolve the one exported definition of that name in the test crate. Spec cell: RIPR-SPEC-0117 example 10 (#10298).
